# Context (public sources only)

This page places the work in its public context. Every statement about a real instrument or body below is a row of `data/evidence_table.csv`: a paraphrase of a source that was retrieved and read during the research phase, with its access level and URL. Nothing here quotes a standard or a paywalled text. Rows are leads to confirm in the source (see `docs/REPORT.md` section 2.3 on the verification error rate).

No body named here, and no other body, has reviewed, requested or endorsed this work. The repository is a student proposal seed. It uses no logo, seal, colour scheme or official wording of any authority.

## Why Gulf conditions

The evidence table was searched for any instrument that requires a ground robot to be tested against Gulf heat, dust, glare, or GNSS jamming or spoofing. None was found. The closest hooks are drone rules, road vehicle rules and general test methods, listed below. The Gulf protocol (`docs/GULF_TEST_PROTOCOL.md`) and the simulation (`docs/EVALUATION.md`) start from that gap.

## Who might read this

The intended readers are research, technology and public sector innovation bodies in the UAE that work on autonomous systems. They are not named in this repository, because none has been contacted and naming them could suggest an endorsement that does not exist. A short enquiry pack for the open regulatory question is in `docs/UAE_ENQUIRY_PACK.md`; nothing has been sent.

## Reading (interpretation)

- The legally binding layer found for UAE autonomy is drone heavy, plus road vehicle rules in Dubai that list autonomous equipment and machinery among the covered categories. No rule for an indoor service robot was found; this is a statement about the search, not about the law.
- GNSS interference is recognised in public UAE working papers to the international civil aviation body, but none of the sources sets a test for ground robots.
- EU instruments matter only if a product is placed on the EU market; they are listed because buyers and insurers may still ask for their style of evidence.
